before: This Praxis builds and evaluates CyberSentinel, a cascaded uniform resource locator (URL) phishing detector combining structural classification, a character transformer and distribution monitoring. Paired experiments answer three research questions about representation, monitoring and inline execution. Structural features improve internal recall by 64.07 percentage points; validation controls identify a strong format–class association that qualifies transfer. Forcing Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS) under fixed weights reduces external false positives from 2,261 to 50 and gold detections from 69 to 22, directly measuring scheme sensitivity. Monitoring recognizes 87.12% of external windows, while its escalation adds 218 false positives without another gold detection. Paired model decisions establish a 90.5487% false-positive floor for selection between unchanged decisions on the evaluated cohort. Supporting service experiments reduce median paired 95th-percentile latency by 79.68% through worker-owned clients in single-host synthetic structural-only Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) measurements, with a no-model control supporting the client-path explanation. The contribution is a reproducible evaluation connecting representation choices, useful expert corrections, monitoring actions and execution costs to gateway design.
after: This Praxis establishes an empirical design basis for cascaded uniform resource locator (URL) phishing detection through CyberSentinel, a system combining structural classification, a character transformer and distribution monitoring. Three research questions connect representation, monitoring and selective execution to detection quality and service cost. Paired cross-dataset comparisons, controlled input interventions and service measurements explain how these design choices affect system behavior. Structural features increase internal recall by 64.07 percentage points. Validation controls reveal a strong association between URL format and class labels, while fixed-weight interventions establish sensitivity to scheme spelling. Together, these findings identify representation dependence without assigning an unmeasured share of the internal gain to format. Paired model outputs establish a 90.5487% false-positive floor for routing between unchanged decisions on the evaluated external cohort, making the expert’s available corrections a measurable design constraint. Monitoring detects 87.12% of external windows, while escalation adds 218 false positives without additional gold-positive detections, demonstrating the importance of evaluating alerts through their resulting decisions. Controlled service experiments identify an effective implementation change: worker-owned clients reduce median paired 95th-percentile latency by 79.68% in single-host synthetic structural-only measurements, with a no-model control supporting the client-path explanation. The resulting contribution is concrete engineering guidance: evaluate representation stability alongside detection, select experts for useful corrections, measure monitoring through response outcomes, and target execution costs identified by controlled measurement.
